blocks.text: The chapter’s references to Assyria, Egypt, agreements, wealth, oppression, and judgment belong to the northern kingdom’s later imperial crisis. Hosea sets these present pressures alongside Israel’s remembered story: Jacob, the exodus, life in tents, and prophetic guidance. This reuse of earlier traditions diagnoses a present failure of identity and calls for change. The critique of alliances and rulers addresses destructive power, elite exploitation, war, and misplaced security; it should not be turned into a prescription for a modern party or state policy.

sections.title: Reading Hosea’s Political and Historical References
